newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hits high on Mississippi news, eases bac.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hits high on Mississippi news, eases bac.

text.p: IPE Brent crude hit a new session high in early afternoon trade on Thursday, helped by further disruption to shipping on the Mississippi River, before easing back toward mid-range, brokers said.
May Brent touched a high of $20.42 a barrel before slipping back to $20.22, 10 cents down on the day but seven cents off the low by 1548 GMT.
"(The rally) was probably due to the Mississippi news but there's very little volume going through," said a broker.
Marine traffic on the Mississippi River, already hampered by a capsized barge, was closed to vessels in two other areas.
The U.S. Coast Guard said the river at Baton Rouge was open during daylight hours to north- and south-bound traffic on a one-way, one vessel at a time basis.
Dealers said concern about the prospect of disruption to product supplies helped push NYMEX prices higher but essentially the market remained range-bound.
"Brent is still stuck in a range between $20.07 and $20.50," said one.
"Part of the early gains this afternoon were due to the fact that we managed to hold eight cents off the low end (of the range) during the morning," he added.
IPE prompt gas oil, meanwhile, was $2.50 lower at $172.75 a tonne by 1557 GMT, just 25 cents above the session low.
Dealers saw good support for April gas oil at $172.00.
